abstract: Adiabatic quantum computing (AQC) is based on the adiabatic principle, where a quantum system remains in an instantaneous eigenstate of the driving Hamiltonian. The final state of the Hamiltonian encodes solution to the problem of interest. While AQC has distinct advantages, recent researches have shown that quantumness such as quantum coherence in adiabatic processes may be lost entirely due to the system-bath interaction when the evolution time is long, and consequently the expected quantum speedup dose not show up. Here we propose a fast-signal assisted adiabatic quantum algorithm. We find that by applying a sequence of fast random or regular signals during the evolution process, the runtime can be reduced greatly, yet advantages of the adiabatic algorithm remain intact. Significantly, we present a randomized Trotter formula and show that the driving Hamiltonian and the sequence of fast signals can be implemented simultaneously. We apply the algorithm for solving the $3$-bit exact cover problem (EC$3$) and put forward an approach for implementing the problem with trapped ions.

specification.problem: Fast-signal assisted adiabatic quantum algorithm: apply a sequence of fast random or regular signals during adiabatic evolution to shorten runtime (limiting decoherence) while keeping adiabatic advantages. A randomized Trotter formula lets the driving Hamiltonian and the fast signals be implemented simultaneously. Applied to the 3-bit exact cover problem (EC3), with a proposed trapped-ion implementation.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction only: generic adiabatic evolution with a driving Hamiltonian, a fast-signal term, and a randomized Trotter decomposition, plus an EC3 final Hamiltonian as a finite instance. Specific signal forms, couplings, schedules, and ion-trap pulse details are not given in the abstract.

registers.name: q
registers.role: system qubits encoding the bit string of the EC3 problem

specification.initial_state: Uniform superposition |+>^{\otimes n}, the ground state of H_0=-\sum_i X_i (assumed standard choice)

steps.description: Prepare the system qubits in the ground state of H_0.
Discretize [0,T] into short steps; define the total Hamiltonian as the adiabatic interpolation plus fast signals.
In each step apply a randomly sampled Trotter term so driving and signal parts are implemented simultaneously.
Continue until s=1 so the state approximates the ground state of H_P.

specification.measurement: At t=T measure all n system qubits in the computational (Z) basis, repeated over many runs (and random signal realizations); the outcome bit strings sample the approximate ground state of H_P.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Take the most frequent outcome (or lowest H_P energy among outcomes) as the candidate solution, and classically check it against the EC3 clauses (exactly one true bit per clause). Success probability is estimated from the outcome frequencies.
